text: A real environment is rarely one module — it's several, each responsible for one layer. This lesson composes three: the network module from Lesson 14, a new compute module for a VM and its network interface, and a database module for a SQL server and its firewall rule, wired together into one buildable environment.

Each module is written the same way Lesson 14 wrote network — its own variables.tf, main.tf, and outputs.tf — and each one can still be tested on its own, with its own made-up inputs, independent of the other two. network knows nothing about compute, and compute knows nothing about database; the wiring between them lives entirely in the root configuration.

compute needs somewhere to put its network interface, and network already produced exactly that: subnet_id equals module.network.subnet_ids at index zero. No subnet ID is typed in by hand anywhere, so it can never drift out of sync with whatever network actually created. Because compute's input directly references network's output, Terraform's dependency graph already knows network has to be created first.

The same pattern chains a second time: database needs to know which IP address its firewall should allow in, and allowed_ip equals module.compute.private_ip means that rule is always built from the VM's actual private IP, whatever it turns out to be, instead of a value someone guessed and hard-coded ahead of time.

Three apply-worthy resources come up from one terraform apply, in the right order, with no depends_on written anywhere — the reference from one module's input to another's output is the dependency. That's the same module block and the same module-dot-output syntax from Lesson 14, just used three times and chained together.

What makes this work at scale is that each module still does exactly one job and stays independently testable, the same way testing one PowerShell function in isolation beats running an entire script to see if one piece works. Chapter 5 picks up from here: running this same composed environment against dev, staging, and prod using Terraform workspaces.
